name: Immediate play
requirement: A new player can enter robot choice and the first puzzle without account, age entry, purchase, download wall or compulsory text tutorial.

name: Choose a robot
requirement: Four visibly robotic starter characters are freely selectable, cosmetic-only and interchangeable without resetting progress.

name: World and level discovery
requirement: World cards and numbered level nodes show completed, available, upcoming and offline-unavailable states distinctly.

name: Visual program editor
requirement: Add, insert, reorder, replace, remove, clear and undo command blocks with deterministic program order and visible capacity.

name: Equivalent input methods
requirement: Every programming action works with touch drag, tap-to-place and keyboard; no hover-only or drag-only essential action.

name: Run control
requirement: Run, pause, resume, single-step and reset show exactly the authoritative execution trace; editing is disabled while playing.

name: Helpful outcomes
requirement: Success, collision, unfinished route, action limit and invalid-program states have different, non-shaming feedback and preserve the draft.

name: Explicit constraints
requirement: Program blocks and executed actions are separate limits. The full AST counts for blocks; each primitive action costs one action.

name: Bounded repeat
requirement: World 2 introduces repeat 2–5 times with a nonempty primitive-only body. No nested, conditional or infinite loops in v1.

name: Switches and gates
requirement: World 3 introduces auto-triggered floor switches that permanently open named gates for the current attempt; reset closes them.

name: Progressive discovery
requirement: Short skippable visual demonstrations introduce only the next needed command and can be replayed on demand.

name: Gentle hints
requirement: Authored hints progress from goal cue to spatial cue to command-pattern cue; no timers, payment or reward penalties.

name: Transparent ratings
requirement: Each level earns up to three persistent stars for completion, collecting all bonus stars and meeting the block target; best awards never decrease.

name: Lightweight rewards
requirement: Earn badges and cosmetic accents from completion milestones; no currency, loot boxes, streak pressure, character power or paid hints.

name: Local progress
requirement: Save the robot, settings, drafts and best results locally; export, validated import and erase are available in the grown-up area.

name: Honest offline play
requirement: Shell and confirmed-downloaded worlds work offline. Missing packs are unavailable, not incorrectly labeled locked or ready.

name: Responsive interface
requirement: Play at 360 CSS pixels wide and above, with portrait, landscape, tablet and desktop arrangements and safe-area support.

name: Accessible play
requirement: Provide semantic controls, visible focus, motion reduction, non-color signals, accessible program order and an equivalent textual board explorer.

name: Audio and motion
requirement: Animation and sound reinforce outcomes but are never required; sound starts only after interaction and settings persist.

name: Data-driven content
requirement: Versioned JSON defines worlds, robots, levels and programs; no special case based on a level ID in the simulator.

name: Substantial level library
requirement: Public v1 contains 60 authored levels in four 15-level worlds, with a six-level first playable slice and documented diversity review.

name: Content validation
requirement: Every released level has schema checks, semantic checks, replayable witnesses and tested three-star attainability; proof claims are bounded.

name: Child-focused privacy
requirement: No child accounts, personal profiles, advertising, chat, trackers or remote gameplay analytics in v1; hosting data practices require human review.

name: Settings and grown-up area
requirement: Expose sound, reduced motion, replay tutorial and storage controls; protect destructive actions with explicit confirmation, not a false consent claim.

name: Recovery
requirement: Interrupted runs, corrupt saves, asset errors, storage denial, multiple tabs and graphics loss recover without silently awarding or erasing progress.

name: Localization readiness
requirement: English is the v1 content language; all user text uses locale keys, supports expansion and avoids language baked into game assets.

name: Safe parsing and delivery
requirement: Reject malformed, oversized or incompatible content and imports; never eval program data or accept arbitrary asset/script URLs.

name: Evidence-led quality
requirement: Use headless rule tests, component interaction tests, browser journeys, manual accessibility review and recorded physical-device measurements.

name: Controlled release
requirement: Deploy immutable static builds with tested base paths, cache lifecycle, compatible saves and rollback; public release requires human sign-off.

name: Learning validation
requirement: Conduct guardian-consented formative playtests and examine independent command use, retry behavior and puzzle diversity without claiming proven learning gains.
